summary:
The core holds up when checked against the tree. Every change that would have rejected an unchecked file at or after the cutoff gets the same watermark, because ProbePass.Run returns Cancelled on every path and SizeBatch applies nothing when it does (Scanner.cs:507-514). The range walk is correct for depth-first registration with one block per folder. AtLeast is a true lower bound. The AtLeast-equals-rolled contract also holds for file entries, since RolledSize of a file is its ChargedSize (ScanStore.Rollup.cs:19-24). The choice of an init-only property keeps the SL-100 reflection tests that call `.Single()` on the TopLevelSnapshot constructor compiling.

Two major problems:
- **The design contradicts a decided question.** Q-283, answered after the design was written, changes the listing-Stop header. The design keeps it byte for byte and pins it through L-001 and the L-004 check.
- **The real-tree sweep cases do not fit the engine's 120 s case limit (Q-222).** A 60 s bound per Fact does not keep case commands under 120 s when they select two or three rows plus a build. The named restale recipe also spawns a cmd.exe mklink for every group before every scan.

Minor problems:
- Two invariants are held by remembering rather than by construction. The watermark is recorded only on the Cancelled branch instead of being advanced on each commit, and nothing seals the store after the scan's last write. The second is this design's unproven must-verify precondition.
- One case shape (the queued batch) is not reached deterministically by its triggers.
- One wind-down row has no teeth.
- No case runs the rules harness that Q-027 requires for a fitness.yaml change.
- L-004's 60,000-file fixture has no sweep for runs the engine kills.
- The StoppedInSizeChecks flag is never asserted in Core.
- The storeBackup citation says the opposite of what its source says.
- Q-283's own sentence and the kept 'are short' clause both disagree with measurements; this is reported for a person to settle.

findings.claim: Q-283 (decided after this design) requires the listing-Stop header to also say unmarked rows may be off. The design keeps it byte-identical ('Listing-Stop headers stay byte-identical, so L-001 and $StoppedListHeader keep passing'), and L-004's check command runs L-001 expecting the old string. Built as designed, the slice contradicts a decided question. The design also leaves an uncovered edge Q-283 fixes. A Stop at the last AfterFolder returns Cancelled with every folder listed and SizeFiles never run, so _uncheckedFrom is 0 and StoppedInSizeChecks is false. The old listing header then says only marked rows are short while no row is marked and no file was checked.
findings.evidence: Q-283 decision text; design key_decisions 'Derived criterion 8...' rationale; L-004 case check `-Case L-004; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { ... -Case L-001 }`; WindowCases.ps1:1290 (L-001 literal) and :6320 ($StoppedListHeader, used at :6570/:6575 by the stopped-view switching helper); Scanner.cs:227-228 (FolderDone stop returns Finish(Cancelled) before SizeFiles)
findings.fix: Add Q-283's change to the Final, non-sizing arm of ListHeader. Edit L-001's literal and $StoppedListHeader to the new string, and keep L-004's sizing-arm string distinct. Rerun the cases that use $StoppedListHeader, plus WindowMutants -Mutant All (Q-114). For the wording, see m1.

findings.claim: The time bound does not match the engine's case limit. Each Fact is bounded at 'under 60 s', but the case commands select several rows. The 'StopsInThe' filter (cases 5-7) runs the listing Fact plus both rows of the sizing Theory. Cases 2, 3 and 8 run the two-row Theory. Case 4 adds NothingChangesOnceTheScanHasReturned. Each command also runs `eng/dotnet.ps1 test`'s build. So a command can take 120-180 s plus build, past Q-222's 120 s job kill. A killed case stays 'named' and is never 'covered' (SL-098's C-002/C-003 pattern), and its TempTree leaks. The named restale recipe makes this likely. It is the CancellationTests recipe ('TempTree.Hardlink and TempTree.Append'), and TempTree.Hardlink spawns cmd.exe mklink per link. Re-creating 8 groups before every scan (2 references, every AfterFolder point, sampled guarded calls, and 2 worker counts × several sizing stop kinds) adds 8 process spawns per scan.
findings.evidence: Q-222 (repro.py TIMEOUT = 120 s, whole job killed); design cases 2-8 filters; component 'Real-tree stop sweeps' ('Each Fact prints its elapsed time and must stay under 60 s'; 'Restale() re-creates every group before every scan'); CancellationTests.cs:186-187; spike stop-pending-checks restaled by resizing ('stale length through the first name, true length through a later name'), not by re-linking.
findings.fix: Bound each case command, not each Fact. Keep every row at 25 s or less so the largest filter, build included, stays under about 90 s, or point cases 5-7 at a single row. Create the hardlinks once when the tree is built. Restale by SetLength through the first name, then through a later name, with no mklink per scan. Settle it by running each case command once on the built tree and recording its elapsed time.

findings.claim: The decided header text disagrees with measurements in two places, and a person has to settle it. (1) Q-283's literal sentence says only 'Other rows' on-disk sizes ... may be off'. Survey run A measured 3-shrink's logical size above final too: (64 MiB, 64 MiB, 1) stopped against (1 MiB, 1 MiB, 1) final. (2) Q-283 keeps 'Rows marked not read yet or stopped partway are short'. The at-least spike measured the un-subtracted listed figure above the reference in 20,998 unfinished folders, so a stopped-partway row holding a stale-large first name is not short. The design's sizing-arm wording ('may be off, on disk especially') is consistent with (1). Nothing in the design addresses (2).
findings.evidence: Q-283 decision; survey runs A/B; spike at-least-figures-5m-within-budget real sweep ('The un-subtracted listed figure exceeded the reference in 20,998 of those unfinished folders')
findings.fix: Use Q-283's permitted alternative, the sizing-Stop wording ('may be off, on disk especially'), for the Done-row clause. Raise the 'are short' clause with a person rather than building it as true. SC-393's at-least figures are what would make it true.

quote.text: $StoppedListHeader = 'What was read before the stop. Rows marked not read yet or stopped partway are short.'

findings.claim: The watermark is recorded only on one exit. _uncheckedFrom is set inside SizeBatch's Cancelled branch and is otherwise 0. A later `return false` added anywhere else in SizeFiles (for example a cancellation check between batches, a natural edit) would leave the watermark at 0. That marks every already-probed file pending, makes every folder unfinished, and turns StoppedInSizeChecks false, so a sizing Stop shows the listing header. Nothing fails. The invariant 'the watermark is the first unapplied entry' holds by remembering, not by construction. The design names Jim Gray's applied-up-to watermark, which is advanced on every commit rather than recorded at the failure.
findings.evidence: Design component 'Scanner records where the checks stopped' ('SizeBatch sets _uncheckedFrom = entries[0] when pass.Run returns Cancelled')
findings.fix: Make the field an advancing cursor. Set it to the first due entry when sizing starts, and to entries[count-1]+1 after each batch is applied. Finish writes Count when Completed and the cursor otherwise. Every way out of SizeFiles then leaves the right cutoff, and StoppedInSizeChecks stays `Cancelled && _uncheckedFrom > 0`.

findings.claim: The design's one must-verify precondition, 'nothing writes the store after Scanner.Scan returns, including the watermark', is held by remembering. The fitness fence limits which file may call EndSizeChecks, not when. No store writer refuses a call after it. If it fails (a future resume path, a late apply of an abandoned batch, or Core analysis code calling CorrectSizes or SetChildren on a returned store), Unfinished and AtLeast change while the stopped results are open, and a folder already reported final can move. Criterion 5 breaks with no error. NothingChangesOnceTheScanHasReturned only samples two scenarios.
findings.evidence: Design cross_domain_transfer invariant 4 (status must-verify); contract 'Stop has taken effect'
findings.fix: Have EndSizeChecks also seal the store. Append, AppendRoot, SetChildren, AddFlags and CorrectSizes then throw InvalidOperationException once it is set; VolumeUsed is untouched. Tests may still call EndSizeChecks repeatedly on a synthetic store they no longer append to. The regex fence then matters less.

findings.claim: Case 2's shape, 'so pass.Run returns Cancelled before probing', is not reached by the triggers it names. 'Cancel at the first probe of a batch' fires from the Probe seam on a worker thread after Run has started the workers, so it lands on the mid-batch path. The FilesSized boundary poller races the scan thread, which builds the next 8-entry batch and calls Run in microseconds. No seam runs on the scan thread between one batch's apply and the next Run: AfterFolder is listing-only and Probe runs inside Run. The early return is therefore hit only by chance, and the floor 'each stop kind occurs at least once' counts triggers, not landings (CC-005).
findings.evidence: ScanOptions.cs (seams: AfterFolder listing-only, Probe on workers); design case 2 shape and the sweep's non-vacuity floors
findings.fix: Either record the landing and floor on it (no Probe-seam call for the batch whose first entry is the watermark), or reword the shape to the mid-batch and boundary-race landings actually reached. The watermark is the same on either path, so no component changes.

findings.claim: The listing row of NothingChangesOnceTheScanHasReturned cannot fail. After a listing Stop no thread outlives Scan: no probe pass ran, and the canceller and the Run are disposed before return. Comparing the store at return with the store 200 ms later is therefore vacuous. The FolderDone-after-Cancel commit the case's 'why' names happens before the first snapshot, so the row does not check it.
findings.evidence: Design case 'nothing changes once Stop has taken effect' (shape and why); Scanner.cs:378-417
findings.fix: Drop the row. If coverage of the commit-after-Cancel path is wanted, assert instead that the folder whose listing returned cleanly after Cancel reads listed and its checked-kind files read SizeCheckPending (watermark 0).

findings.claim: The slice adds a settled rule to .taad/fitness.yaml, but no case runs the rules harness or RuleCases. Q-027 (human) requires eng/rules-harness/harness.py at validate for slices that change .taad/fitness.yaml (lessons #486, #504). No row shows the rule fires on an EndSizeChecks call in another src file, so a mis-scoped files or except_files entry would pass silently. RuleCases' settled count is now derived (RuleCases.ps1:344-366), so no count needs editing; the run is still owed.
findings.evidence: Q-026/Q-027 decisions; design architecture_rules; design cases (none for the rule)
findings.fix: Add one case: the harness command from lesson #106 at the slice's tree, plus `tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001` and `-Case C-003`. Add a fire row (a plant calling EndSizeChecks under src/FsAnalyser.Core/Analysis) and a quiet row (the call in Scanner.cs).

quote.text:
# settled by SL-112
  - name: only the scan's ending writes the size-check watermark
    files: src/**/*.cs
    must_not_match:
    - \bEndSizeChecks\b

findings.claim: L-004 creates at least 60,000 files. The only case-folder helper roots under GetTempPath(), which is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP in engine shells, where Remove-Item is refused (lesson #360). Its cleanup is a finally that never runs when Q-222's 120 s kill fires, and nothing sweeps orphaned roots. A killed run therefore leaves 60k files that later %TEMP% and C:\ scans count (lesson #333). The case is also close to the cap: a publish when the exe is stale, building the 60k-file fixture, then the scan (lesson #503: comparable cases take 60-75 s).
findings.evidence: Design component 'Window check of the sizing-Stop header'; CC-009; Remove-CaseFolder (WindowCases.ps1:329-333) uses Remove-Item
findings.fix: Give L-004 a %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp root with a per-run GUID, a start-of-case sweep of earlier L-004 roots, and [IO.Directory]::Delete for cleanup. Time the case once and record it against 120 s.

findings.claim: StoppedInSizeChecks decides which header the App shows, but only end-to-end window cases check it: L-004 for true and L-001 for false. No Core Fact asserts it. The edges are a Stop at the last AfterFolder (every folder listed, no batch run: must be false), a Stop in the sizing pass under the stuck-worker abandon path (true), and Completed (false). A wrong condition in Finish would surface only through a slow window case.
findings.evidence: Design component 'Final snapshot says the Stop landed in the size checks'; the sweeps already produce every one of these endings
findings.fix: In both sweep Facts and AScanThatRunsToTheEndMarksNothing, assert result.TopLevel?.StoppedInSizeChecks == (status is Cancelled && the stop landed in SizeFiles), with the last-AfterFolder Stop included in the listing sweep.

findings.claim: The cited prior art says an interrupted storeBackup 'is reported as such, not as finished'. The cited page says the opposite: 'If you have interrupted backups, they are simply broken and also ``finished'' in this sense.' The page does support the first half (complete means no late links left to set). Nothing in the design rests on it, but the record carries a citation its source contradicts.
findings.evidence: https://www.nongnu.org/storebackup/en/node74.html ('This means, there are absolutely no ``late-links'' to set ... If you have interrupted backups, they are simply broken and also ``finished'' in this sense.')
findings.fix: Restate the prior art as 'a backup with late links still to set is not complete (storeBackup node74)' and drop the clause about interrupted backups, or cite node75 ('the last (unfinished) backup is not a full backup').

dimensions_checked.result:
Code claims checked against the tree and all hold:
- Finish is expression-bodied (Scanner.cs:568).
- SizeFiles walks 1..Count-1 ascending and returns true when nothing is due (:446-502).
- SizeBatch applies nothing from a Cancelled batch (:507-514).
- A Stop in the listing returns before SizeFiles runs (:205-228).
- ProbeRule is set only by HeldOpenTreeTests, with CancellationToken.None (:255).
- TopLevelSnapshot has a single internal constructor, which the SL-100 tests reflect with .Single().
- L-004 is unused.
- FSA_HOOK_AT_SIZED fires on the 'Reading each file's own size: ' line (StartupHook.cs:722-731).

Two findings:
- m9: the storeBackup citation is contradicted by its source.
- m1: Q-283's wording and its kept clause disagree with the survey and the spike.

The recalled WAL/LSN and nested-set prior art is decorative. The recalled ACL claim is not load-bearing.

Edges that do hold:
- Count-0 stores (Refused, Stop in calls 1-2): EndSizeChecks(0) is accepted.
- due==0 gives Completed with the watermark at Count.
- Vanished files: the watermark, not the flags, decides.
- NotListed later siblings and page-straddling blocks are handled by the range walk.

One edge was found: a Stop at the last AfterFolder (every folder listed, no checks) leaves the flag false, and the old listing header then misleads. It is folded into M1, because Q-283 fixes it.

m2: the watermark is recorded only on the Cancelled branch rather than advanced on each commit.

m3: no seal on store writes after the scan's last write. The must-verify precondition therefore holds by remembering.

The preorder/one-SetChildren dependency is inherited from SL-111. It cannot be enforced cheaply at the store and is recorded and filed.

None significant. Only the R read form was taken; no P pass, per-entry bit or pending set. The fitness fence costs harness runs for an internal method that a store seal (m3) would mostly subsume. Not raised separately.

None beyond the header. AtLeast equals (RolledSize, RolledOnDisk, FilesBelow) for files as well, because RolledSize of a file is its ChargedSize (ScanStore.Rollup.cs:19-24). EndSizeChecks accepts 0..Count inclusive, so Count-0 results work. StoppedInSizeChecks semantics match Q-111.

None. The values passed to EndSizeChecks are always in range (entries[0] < Count, 0, or Count). A worker fault throws out of Scan before Finish, so no store is handed out. The ArgumentOutOfRangeException on an empty store is filed for the App (lesson #517).
M1: the design keeps the listing-Stop header unchanged against Q-283's newer decision. The Q-160 assumption the design reports as false (Done-row sizes complete) is correctly not built.

M2: case commands exceed Q-222's 120 s limit, and restaling relies on cmd.exe mklink.

m6: the rules harness required by Q-027 has no case.

m7: L-004's fixture has no orphan sweep (CC-009).

Q-114's WindowMutants requirement is acknowledged by the design. T-003 is correctly not required (Q-128).

m4: the queued-batch shape is not reached deterministically.

m5: the listing wind-down row is vacuous.

m8: StoppedInSizeChecks is not asserted in Core.

Criteria 1-7 each have a material case. The teeth and non-vacuity floors on the sweep are sound.
None. No new file opens, writes, elevation or exposed data. The new public reads expose only figures the store already exposes.
